source.description: Carries each package's source hash to its dependents, so a check reruns when a package it loads changes, without waiting for that package's checks.

typecheck.description: pnpm types: each project checked incrementally, from the build info its last build left. toolchain-typecheck -b (tsrs -b) builds the package's project and the projects it references, so it runs after theirs. Its outputs are types/: the declarations and the build info they were built from (tsconfig tsBuildInfoFile), so a cache hit restores both together and the next build compares the sources against the declarations on disk.

typecheck:full.description: pnpm check's typecheck: each project checked from nothing, never from build info, since an incremental build can keep a diagnostic or a declaration a clean one would not (microsoft/TypeScript#64386, #64591). A package's removes its types/ and builds its own project alone (tsrs -p), against the declarations its references' full builds wrote, so it runs after theirs and writes nothing of theirs.

@bjornpagen/grizzle-pg#typecheck:full.description: The pin's package checks with --noEmit and --incremental false: no build info is read or written, so there is no output.

oxlint.description: The toolchain's preset and plugins (vendor/toolchain) are inputs too.

//#typecheck.description: The tooling project (test, bench, scripts) builds after both packages' projects, which toolchain-typecheck -b then finds up to date; its build info is tsconfig.tsbuildinfo, beside its tsconfig. A root task's inputs are the whole repository, the packages and the toolchain included; the root checks but format read no Markdown, so theirs leave it out.

//#typecheck:full.description: The tooling project checked alone and from nothing (tsrs -p --incremental false), against the declarations both packages' full builds wrote. It writes nothing.

//#workspace-gate.description: The toolchain's repository-wide checks (workspace-gate): every tsconfig's Effect plugin block and diagnostics, the Effect-free package's tsconfig and manifest, and the tree's file names, read as JSON and git's file list, never a TypeScript program. Uncached: it reads the whole tree in about a second, which a cache would have to hash.

//#load.description: toolchain-test load: every test module the runner includes loaded apart, each in a process of its own, failing on one that throws as it loads (a const read in its temporal dead zone, an initializer that throws, an export that is no property). Uncached by turbo: toolchain-test keeps each module's pass by its closure hash, so a check loads only what changed.

//#dedupe.description: pnpm dedupe --check reads the manifests, the lockfile and what they install, never source.
